name: Functional Fixedness
description: Once an object or interface element is strongly associated with its usual function, people can struggle to see other possible uses. Familiar purpose becomes a cognitive constraint on creative problem solving.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to ideation, redesign work, cross-platform adaptation, and product discovery. Teams can inherit old metaphors or components so strongly that they miss better affordances or new uses entirely.
prevalence_note: Frequently taught in design-thinking, innovation, and workshop contexts; less universal in routine UI review, but still a recognizable concept in product and service design.

findings.description: Repeating classic problem-solving experiments, Adamson found that prior exposure to an object's customary function reduced participants' ability to repurpose it for a novel solution. Conventional use framing can therefore become a real obstacle to creative problem solving.
findings.source_title: Functional fixedness as related to problem solving: a repetition of three experiments.

applications.title: Invision repurposing the right-click on its own logo to offer a logo download
applications.description: Invision's website breaks the conventional expectation that right-clicking an image only shows a generic browser context menu -- right-clicking the company's own logo triggers a custom popup offering the logo in multiple downloadable formats, repurposing a familiar interaction for a use most sites never consider.
applications.ethical_note: A pure usability/convenience innovation with no persuasion angle -- repurposing an underused interaction to save users a trip to a buried press-kit page benefits the user directly, with no influence on a purchase or behavioral decision.
